security_audit.summary: Most SKILL.md detections are markdown examples or inline spreadsheet guidance, not execution. The real risks are recalc.py writing a persistent LibreOffice macro and invoking soffice on user files. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Use an isolated temporary LibreOffice user profile for recalculation and delete it after the run.

remediation.issue: Headless LibreOffice execution on user workbooks
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation for recalculation, keep timeouts, and validate workbook paths before invoking soffice.

remediation.issue: Documentation mixes examples with executable workflow
remediation.suggestion: Document the local profile change and explain that recalc.py runs external LibreOffice commands.

finding_verdicts.reason: This starts LibreOffice from PATH to initialize user profile state before macro setup. The arguments are hardcoded and shell injection is unlikely, but the external process changes local application state.
This only runs gtimeout --version with hardcoded arguments to detect a timeout helper. It uses no shell and no user-controlled arguments.

This runs LibreOffice headlessly on a user-supplied workbook path and invokes an application macro. The argument list avoids shell injection, but external document processing and file mutation are real risks.
The URL appears inside an XML namespace for an OpenOffice script module. It is not used for any network request or data transfer.
The script targets the hidden LibreOffice profile under the user home directory. Writing there persists outside the workbook and can affect future LibreOffice behavior.
The same hidden LibreOffice profile path is accessed for macro setup. This is expected for the feature, but it is still a sensitive filesystem location.
The script writes Module1.xba into the LibreOffice profile. The macro content is fixed, but it creates persistent application-level macro code.
The script creates the LibreOffice macro directory in the user profile if it does not exist. This is intentional, but it mutates local application configuration.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent LibreOffice Macro Installation
semantic_findings.description: recalc.py writes Module1.xba into the user LibreOffice profile and later invokes it as an application macro. This persists outside the target workbook and changes local application state.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The macro path, file write, and macro invocation are all present in recalc.py. The macro body is fixed, so the finding concerns persistence and application state rather than exfiltration.

content.value_statement: Spreadsheet work often needs formulas, formatting, and validation across many sheets. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through reliable XLSX creation and analysis.
actual_capabilities: Read Excel, CSV, and TSV data with pandas for analysis.
Create new XLSX workbooks with formulas and formatting.
Modify existing workbooks while preserving formulas and styles.
Apply financial model formatting conventions for inputs and formulas.
Run workbook formula recalculation through the included recalc.py script.
Report spreadsheet formula errors with sheet and cell locations.
limitations: Formula recalculation depends on LibreOffice being available locally.
The recalculation helper changes the local LibreOffice user profile.
Very large workbooks may require memory-conscious pandas or openpyxl options.
The skill provides workflow guidance, not a replacement for spreadsheet review.

use_cases.title: Build Operational Reports
use_cases.description: Create workbooks with clean tabs, formulas, formatting, and source notes for recurring reporting.

use_cases.title: Review Financial Models
use_cases.description: Check formulas, references, assumptions, and formatting before sharing an Excel model.

use_cases.title: Convert Data Into Workbooks
use_cases.description: Load CSV or TSV data, transform it with pandas, and export a formatted XLSX file.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Workbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Excel workbook from this data. Add clear headers, simple formulas, and readable formatting.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Uploaded Spreadsheet
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this workbook. Summarize the sheets, key columns, data quality issues, and useful calculations.

prompt_templates.title: Update an Existing Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Modify this workbook while preserving its formulas and styles. Explain each changed sheet and validation result.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Formula Integrity
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this workbook for formula errors, broken references, inconsistent formulas, and risky hardcoded calculations.

output_examples.input: Create a quarterly sales workbook from regional CSV data.
output_examples.output: A formatted workbook with regional tabs, summary formulas, totals, and source notes.

output_examples.input: Check this financial model for formula problems.
output_examples.output: A review summary listing formula error types, affected cells, and recommended corrections.

output_examples.input: Update this template with new monthly data.
output_examples.output: A revised workbook that preserves existing structure, formatting, formulas, and worksheet conventions.

best_practices: Use formulas for calculated values so workbooks update when inputs change.
Keep assumptions in separate cells and document hardcoded source data.
Recalculate and inspect formula errors before delivering any workbook.
anti_patterns: Do not overwrite formulas by saving a data-only workbook.
Do not apply generic formatting over an established workbook template.
Do not ignore zero, blank, or negative edge cases in formulas.

faq.question: What file types does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on XLSX workbooks and also supports CSV, TSV, and related spreadsheet data workflows.

faq.question: Can it create formulas?
faq.answer: Yes. It instructs the agent to use Excel formulas instead of hardcoded calculated values.

faq.question: Can it preserve existing workbook formatting?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes matching existing templates and preserving styles when editing workbooks.

faq.question: Does formula recalculation require extra software?
faq.answer: Yes. The included recalculation workflow expects LibreOffice to be installed locally.

faq.question: Is this useful for financial models?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes color, number formatting, assumptions, and formula validation guidance for financial models.

faq.question: Does it replace manual spreadsheet review?
faq.answer: No. It helps create and check workbooks, but important files still need human review.
